title: 1744-kellyboost-growth-optimal-portfolio-construction
universal_lens: The KellyBoost primitive unifies portfolio sizing and gradient-boosted trees by defining a pointwise-decoupled loss function. By mapping softmax logits to simplex weights, the negative log-growth rate becomes an exact differentiable objective, establishing a rigorous isomorphism between empirical risk minimization and continuous-time growth-optimal capital allocation.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the CRRA utility dial (γ) to Bayesian posterior tempering. The leave-one-out ensemble stabilizes conformal prediction intervals against single-row perturbations. This ensures that estimated full-Kelly allocations are shrunk toward robust fractional-Kelly priors, preventing overconfident concentration when underlying edge estimates approach statistical noise boundaries.
gse_mapping: GSE treats weekly slate construction as a state-transition on the long-only simplex. The derived diagonal Hessian guides tree splits based on relative asset outperformance. GSE deploys the γ>1 dial to dynamically adjust bankroll exposure, ensuring situational reasoning tempers aggressive Kelly targets during high-variance macro-regimes.

primitives.name: Growth-Optimal Softmax Loss
primitives.verbatim_quote: Per-row loss l_t = -log(1 + w_t^T y_t); the sample mean is the negative log growth rate — the Kelly criterion as a training objective.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: w_t: Portfolio weight vector (dimensionless, simplex), y_t: Realized simple returns vector (dimensionless), l_t: Per-row loss (nats).
primitives.assumptions: Long-only fully-invested simplex constraint; E|log(1+w^T y)| < ∞; i.i.d.-ish rows for pointwise-decoupling.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if 1 + w_t^T y_t ≤ 0 (total capital ruin), rendering the logarithm undefined.

layer2.mapping: Maps standard empirical risk minimization directly to maximizing asymptotic geometric wealth growth under a softmax parameterization.
layer2.telemetry: Realized log growth per decision period.

primitives.name: CRRA Fractional-Kelly Dial
primitives.verbatim_quote: Two deployment stabilizers: (a) a leave-one-out ensemble (K_ens=4 members, each fit on data minus one row, hyperparameters unchanged) because single tree fits are unstable to one-row perturbations (near-tied split flips); (b) a CRRA risk-aversion dial γ (γ→1 recovers log) tunable on the selection protocol.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: γ: Constant Relative Risk Aversion coefficient (dimensionless), S: Competing portfolio return (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Utility function must be strictly concave; γ > 1 implies fractional Kelly behavior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If γ → 0, the model approaches risk-seeking behavior, leading to extreme boundary concentrations and numerical instability.

layer2.mapping: Acts as a mathematical regularizer, shrinking aggressive full-Kelly allocations toward safer fractional-Kelly staking within the optimization kernel.
layer2.telemetry: Max drawdown reduction compared to raw full-Kelly baseline.

primitives.name: Analytic Diagonal Hessian
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Hessian: diagonal h_k can be negative (loss not convex in z); safeguard uses |h_k| since XGBoost leaf weights divide by aggregated Hessian.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: h_k: Diagonal Hessian element (dimensionless), z_k: Logit for asset k (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Twice continuously differentiable loss function with respect to logits.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Negative curvature regions where h_k < 0 require absolute value clipping to prevent inverted gradient updates in second-order optimizers.

layer2.mapping: Enables native integration of the non-convex Kelly objective into XGBoost's Newton-like splitting heuristic via absolute-value stabilization.
layer2.telemetry: Gradient update stability and convergence speed.

reasoning_traces.think:
The KellyBoost framework fundamentally bridges the gap between discrete tabular machine learning and continuous-time financial mathematics. By parameterizing portfolio weights through a softmax function applied to tree-predicted logits, the authors transform the inherently combinatorial portfolio optimization problem into a smooth, differentiable empirical risk minimization task. The core innovation lies in the derivation of the exact gradient and diagonal Hessian for the negative log-growth loss. Unlike standard cross-entropy, which only cares about the argmax label, this loss penalizes the magnitude of misallocated capital across all assets simultaneously. However, the non-convexity of the loss landscape introduces negative curvature in the Hessian, necessitating the absolute-value safeguard to maintain stable Newton-step approximations within the XGBoost architecture. Furthermore, the paper empirically demonstrates that minimizing this loss yields 'full-Kelly' allocations that are excessively concentrated due to estimation error in finite samples. To counteract this, the CRRA dial (γ > 1) is introduced, effectively embedding a fractional-Kelly shrinkage prior directly into the objective function. This dual mechanism—exact growth-optimal gradients tempered by utility-based risk aversion—creates a robust operator for real-world deployment where transaction costs and model uncertainty dominate theoretical asymptotic limits.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive descends from Kelly's 1956 optimal gambling strategy, later adapted to continuous finance by Thorp and Samuelson. The modern lineage connects to end-to-end predict-then-optimize frameworks (e.g., Bartlett et al., 2019) but uniquely solves the non-differentiability of combinatorial simplex constraints via softmax relaxation and exact second-order derivatives for tree ensembles. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a game-theoretic perspective, the market acts as an adversarial agent attempting to exploit overconfident estimators. The KellyBoost model anticipates this by using the CRRA dial to simulate a more conservative opponent, deliberately under-betting on high-edge signals to survive variance traps. The leave-one-out ensemble further models the instability of the market's microstructure, ensuring the policy remains robust to single-event perturbations.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict veto condition applies if the realized returns y_t cause 1 + w_t^T y_t ≤ 0, triggering a logarithmic singularity. Additionally, if the feature pipeline induces severe multicollinearity, the softmax logits may become ill-conditioned, causing the diagonal Hessian approximation to fail. In such regimes, the system must fallback to a flat-staking or independent fractional-Kelly baseline to prevent catastrophic drawdowns.
